title: The ionic model

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ionic bond
items.clue: The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

items.label: Volatility
items.clue: The tendency of a substance to vaporize; low for compounds such as NaCl.

items.label: Ionic lattice
items.clue: A regular, repeating three-dimensional arrangement of cations and anions.

items.label: Electrical conductivity
items.clue: Shown by NaCl only when molten or aqueous, because its ions are then free to move.

questions.stem: An atom of element X has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴. Which ion does X form in its ionic compounds?

options.text: X²⁺
X⁶⁺
X²⁻
X⁶⁻

questions.explanation: X has six outer electrons (3s² 3p⁴). It gains two electrons, giving 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶, and with 16 protons and 18 electrons its charge is 2−. (X is sulfur, which forms S²⁻, as in sodium sulfide, Na₂S.)

questions.stem: Which describes the ionic bonding in solid sodium chloride?

options.text: Attraction between oppositely charged ions in all directions
Transfer of one electron from each sodium atom to a chlorine atom
Attraction joining each Na⁺ to one Cl⁻ in an NaCl molecule
A pair of electrons shared unequally by Na and Cl atoms

questions.explanation: The ionic bond is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions. It is non-directional: each Na⁺ ion attracts all the Cl⁻ ions around it in the lattice, and each Cl⁻ ion attracts all the Na⁺ ions around it.

questions.stem: Copper (atomic number 29) forms both Cu⁺ and Cu²⁺ ions. Which describes how a copper atom forms a Cu²⁺ ion?

options.text: It loses the two electrons from its 4s sublevel.
It loses two 3d electrons and keeps its 4s one.
Its nucleus gains two protons; its electrons stay.
It loses its one 4s electron and one 3d electron.

questions.explanation: Copper is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. The 4s electron is removed first, then one 3d electron, giving Cu²⁺ as [Ar] 3d⁹. Losing only the 4s electron gives Cu⁺, [Ar] 3d¹⁰.

questions.stem: A sample of sodium chloride is made by burning sodium in chlorine. In the solid, each Na⁺ ion has six Cl⁻ ions as its nearest neighbours, all at the same distance. Which statement about the bonding of one Na⁺ ion is correct?

options.text: It is bonded only to the Cl⁻ ion that accepted its electron.
It forms one bond, as its atom had one electron to give.
It is bonded to all six Cl⁻ ions by shared electron pairs.
It is bonded to all six Cl⁻ ions, attracting each of them equally.

questions.explanation: The ionic bond is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions. It depends only on the charges and the distance between the ions, and all six Cl⁻ ions are at the same distance, so the Na⁺ ion is bonded equally to all six.

questions.stem: An iron atom has the electron configuration [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². Iron forms a sulfate with the formula Fe₂(SO₄)₃. What is the electron configuration of the iron ion in this compound? (4s⁰ shows that the 4s sublevel is empty.)

options.text: [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s⁰
[Ar] 3d⁵ 4s⁰
[Ar] 3d³ 4s²
[Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²

questions.explanation: Three sulfate ions carry 3 × (−2) = −6, so the two iron ions carry +6 and each is Fe³⁺. Iron loses its two 4s electrons first and then one 3d electron: [Ar] 3d⁵.

questions.stem: What is the formula of sodium phosphate, with a correct reason?

options.text: Na₃PO₄, as three Na⁺ ions balance one PO₄³⁻ ion
Na₂PO₄, as phosphate has a 2− charge, like sulfate
NaPO₄, as one sodium ion pairs with one phosphate ion
Na(PO₄)₃, as each ion's charge is its own subscript

questions.explanation: Sodium forms Na⁺ and phosphate is PO₄³⁻. Three Na⁺ ions (+3) balance one PO₄³⁻ ion (−3). Only one phosphate ion is needed, so no brackets are used: Na₃PO₄.

questions.stem: Which formula is paired with its correct name?

options.text: Cu₂O, copper(II) oxide
Fe₂O₃, iron trioxide
CuO, copper(II) oxide
CaS, calcium sulfur

questions.explanation: One O²⁻ ion (−2) is balanced by one copper ion, so the copper ion is Cu²⁺ and the Roman numeral is (II).

questions.stem: Which is the correct formula, including its charge, of a polyatomic ion in aqueous solution?

options.text: NH₄⁻(aq)
OH⁻(aq)
NO₃²⁻(aq)
HCO₃²⁻(aq)

questions.explanation: The hydroxide ion is OH⁻. The correct formulas of the other three ions are NH₄⁺ (ammonium), NO₃⁻ (nitrate) and HCO₃⁻ (hydrogencarbonate).

questions.stem: Aluminium, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p¹, reacts with oxygen, 1s² 2s² 2p⁴, to form aluminium oxide. Which gives its formula with a correct reason?

options.text: Al₂O₃, as two Al³⁺ ions cancel the charge of three O²⁻
Al₃O₂, as each ion's charge is written as its own subscript
AlO, as each aluminium ion is paired with one oxide ion
Al₂O, as oxygen has six outer electrons and forms O⁶⁻

questions.explanation: Aluminium loses three electrons to form Al³⁺ and oxygen gains two to form O²⁻. The lowest ratio with zero total charge is 2 × (+3) + 3 × (−2) = 0, so the formula is Al₂O₃.

questions.stem: Which statement about the formula of an ionic compound is correct?

options.text: Ammonium hydrogencarbonate has the chemical formula (NH₄)₂HCO₃
Aluminium phosphate has the chemical formula Al₂(PO₄)₃
Ammonium carbonate has the chemical formula (NH₄)₂CO₃
Potassium phosphate has the chemical formula KPO₄

questions.explanation: Ammonium is NH₄⁺ and carbonate is CO₃²⁻. Two NH₄⁺ ions (+2) balance one CO₃²⁻ ion (−2), and the ammonium ion is kept intact and bracketed.
